title: Record task.cancelled when a retirement or a mission close cancels a task
prompt:
GitHub issue #4: https://github.com/acupof-ai/Spawn/issues/4. Read it, then in crates/spawn-postgres/sql/schema.sql: `spawn_control_apply` (the fold), `spawn_control_refold`, `spawn_task_may_continue`, `spawn_mission_close`, `spawn_resident_retire`, `spawn_task_cancel`, `spawn_task_stages`, and the migration block that records `task.cancelled` for closes from before the closure rule.

The problem. The control stream is the truth, and the `mission_*` tables are its fold. Retiring a resident (`resident.retired`) and closing a mission (`mission.closed`) cancel, in the fold, every task the closure rule does not let go on. They do it by a direct `update mission_tasks set state = 'cancelled'`, with no `task.cancelled` record. So `spawn_task_stages`, which reads only `task.%` records, and therefore `spawn task stages --id N` and every non-web consumer, show a cancelled task whose stages end at `assigned`, `delivered` or `reported`. The web UI hides this by synthesizing a `cancelled` step client-side (`shownStages` in web/src/missions.ts).

What the issue says that needs correcting (line numbers have moved): it is not only a drop. Any `mission.closed` cancels this way, `done` as well as `dropped` (a done mission's assigned work too). The existing migration backfill runs at schema apply and covers only tasks still open that the rule drops. A task already cancelled by the fold is never given its record, by that backfill or by running init-db again. The rest holds.

Required behaviour (the contract the gate checks):
1. Retiring a resident and closing a mission (`dropped` or `done`) leave each task they cancel with exactly one `task.cancelled` control record (`{"type":"task.cancelled","id":<task>}`), so `spawn task stages --id N` ends with the stage `cancelled`.
2. A task the closure rule lets go on (an accepted task of a mission without a gate, for example) gets no such record and keeps its state.
3. The writer appends the records (`spawn_resident_retire` and `spawn_mission_close`, or what they call), never the fold. Folds stay deterministic: rebuilding the tables from the log (`spawn_control_refold()`) gives the same tables and appends nothing, and running `spawn init-db` again adds no record.
4. Remove the client-side synthesis: `shownStages` in web/src/missions.ts and its use in web/src/components/missions/MissionsView.tsx. The stages come from the server.
Also, for databases written before the fix: give each cancelled task whose last `task.%` record is not `task.cancelled` its record once, at migration. It must be idempotent: a task that has one gets no second. Add tests in crates/spawn-postgres/tests/control.rs: after a retirement and after a mission close, the stages end with `cancelled` and there is one record per cancelled task; after `spawn_control_refold()` nothing changes.

The gate judges this with rsi/scenarios/007.sh (read it). A resident with an assigned, a reported and an accepted task is retired. A second mission with an assigned and a reported ephemeral task is dropped. For each of the four cancelled tasks it requires: state `cancelled`, a last stage `cancelled`, and exactly one `task.cancelled` record. For the accepted task: no record and state `accepted`. All of it again after `select spawn_control_refold()` and after `spawn init-db`. It exits 0 when every check passes, 1 when an assertion fails, 2 on a harness failure.

Rules: never edit the protected paths, which the gate rejects: rsi/, scripts/ (scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/, scripts/e2e.sh among them), deploy/, all of web/ except web/src/ and web/index.html, rust-toolchain files and .cargo/. The gate also rejects fewer runnable tests than the base (do not delete, rename, ignore or disable tests), any lint relaxation ([lints] tables, clippy.toml, a new crate-level #![allow]/#![expect], a removed #![warn]/#![deny]) and any build-time code (build.rs, .cargo/, a `build =` key in a Cargo.toml). The gate builds offline from the cargo caches already on the host: a new crate builds only if it is already in ~/.cargo/registry. Keep every existing check green (clippy -D warnings, the workspace tests, the e2e, the black-box scenarios, the web build) and add tests of your own for the new behaviour.
